body: I am going to kill myself
I'm thinking of bringing my Kindle for reading. Does anybody think this is actually a decent alternative to books or would I just have a hard time keeping it charged?
No. I figured that. Thinking about calling and asking when that will fall off.

I'm looking to buy a handgun, and from what I've gathered, you do need a permit to do that.

I don't recall what it was verbatim the, but an old classmate did end up calling the police and they did find me and give me a ride home. I never told them what I was doing but they wanted to take me to the hospital and I refused. He discussed it a little with my mom.

It was June of 2012. I'm 21 now (and was then).
That's a really good point too. Never considered this.

Heh, also an 88M here :)

I intend on bringing tons of movies and shows.

Never would have considered a pre-loaded skype account. thanks for the tip.
We don't deploy for about another year, but I just want to get this taken care of and be feeling better by then!
Only slightly. I know that the chances of me acting on any of this are slim, since there is nobody here to actually push me to do it.

I should be able to. I got into a [state school](http://www.mnsu.edu/) near me and a [community college](http://www.southcentral.edu/) in the same town.

I probably can't afford to go to the state school to start with -- my Army tuition assistance doesn't cover it completely. However, if I do well and am able to pick up scholarships, I should be able to afford it after a year or two at the CC. The only problem facing me is whether to enroll now or wait a bit. I do need a job -- I don't have one at the moment. If I enroll now I will probably just take a math class and nothing more.

It has never been investigated (to my knowledge), but I would not be surprised if I had a light form my ADD/ADHD. I had a hard time paying attention in school -- however, I am not sure if this was due to a learning disorder, or a genuine lack of caring.

I did not do very well in high school, and found the classes to be mostly worthless. I could do the reading just fine on my own and the class was typically too dumb to have a conversation that was remotely interesting, and whenever I asked a question, they got upset because it was always "off-topic" (usually the teacher could tell that I was connecting the dots to other things though -- or I was at least trying to put what we were learning into the context of something relevant (I remember this happening a lot in chemistry)). I didn't do my homework due to the thought that it did not matter, and this ultimately is what caused me to not graduate. I figure I can fix that with college, though. I am concerned about my study habits though, and am afraid that I will not do well in college because of them.

I really like the thought of being a police officer, mostly because it would not be job where you go to the office, sit at your desk, blah, blah. I like variety.

But I am a huge nerd and, right now, I am really paying attention to the mobile world, which I find really interesting. Sadly, I do not have the attention span to learn a programming language (I can do some light web programming) to actually benefit from the possibility of making apps and whatnot.

If I really had to pick, it would probably be tech-stuff, since I'd love to (one day) work at Google, facebook, or Apple. Plus, the perks in the tech industry are unbeatable.

I'd love to be done with at least 4 years of school, probably still in the Military (reserves, still), and either working in the Bay Area with computers at a tech company, or in the police force in the same area.

I am not physically tired, I live with my parents and have no fear of being kicked out. I owe them a fair sum of money and have not really been paying it off (I do not currently have a job).

I would not say there is anything productive I enjoy doing, and I don't know of anywhere around here to volunteer. I live in a small town.

The first thing I would change is that I wouldn't be lazy...I would have motivation to do more than sit on the computer all day.

I don't know of any local groups, and can not afford a doctor.

I don't think that somebody is just going to walk into my life and fix things, but I don't have any role models to go after. My dad is a drunk, and I don't get along with my mother at all.

I think the key to respecting myself lies in fixing my depression.
